title: Guidebook: SIR (Special Intensive Revision)
outlet: Part III Action Research & Resource Centre
shows: Part III Action Research & Resource Centre, a legal aid group in Delhi and Patna, wrote this guide for electors in Delhi and says it grew out of its work helping survivors of domestic violence apply in the revision. It explains what the revision is and who is eligible, how to fill the enumeration form with the booth level officer or online, how to find a name in the draft roll and in Delhi's list of notices, which of Forms 6, 7 and 8 to use, and the documents to keep ready. It goes on to notices, hearings and the two appeals, online and on paper, gives the 1950 helpline and the Commission's complaint routes, and says where to go for help without the internet. It gives Delhi's dates as the Commission revised them on 29 October, with claims and objections until 25 November, notices decided by 15 December and the final roll on 22 December. It sends electors whose enumeration form was not handed in to Form 6 with the declaration, as the Commission's instructions do, and does not take up the Supreme Court's hearing of 28 October, where the bench said electors on the 2026 roll who were left off the draft should be allowed the enumeration form or Form 8 and no order was reported. It also lists Form 7 for an elector whose own name was wrongly deleted, though Form 7 is the form for objecting to a name on the roll, and the Commission's manual sends a person no longer on the roll to Form 6. It is in English and Hindi.
quote: This guide is the result of our experience supporting DV survivors in applying for the SIR (Delhi). It provides a detailed overview of the process, highlights potential challenges you may encounter, and offers practical ways to navigate the same.
note: Shared by the owner as https://share.google/fNIKY7QGWAQOUIFZT, which redirects through https://www.google.com/share.google?q=fNIKY7QGWAQOUIFZT to the post on part-three.org, dated 26 October 2026 (article:published_time 2026-10-26T10:03:29Z, modified 2026-10-30T10:44:48Z), byline 'Part III Team'. The post links the English PDF, https://part-three.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/sir-eng-1.pdf (32 pages, Canva, created 30 October 2026, sha256 3ea72362dd839293b5ba13d5b1e8c3e369d29d51860f6db59e9889820287f00a), read in full with pdftotext on 31 October 2026. A Hindi post and PDF (sir-hindi-1.pdf, 32 pages, created 30 October 2026) carry the same dates. The quote is the opening of the credits page. Delhi's dates in the guide (start 30 June 2026, draft 31 August, claims and objections to 25 November, notice, hearing and disposal to 15 December, final roll 22 December) match the Delhi schedule in data/india/process.json. Its figures of over 97 lakh in the draft and 33.13 lakh notices match the Delhi summary (97,53,577 and 33,12,919). Two points disagree with the sources the site uses, and the summary states both as the guide's. Page 16 and page 18 give Form 7 for 'your name was wrongfully deleted', where the site's help page (remedies.json form7 and form6) has Form 7 as the objection to a name and Form 6 for a person no longer on the roll. Page 17 says an elector whose form was not submitted can apply 'only' on Form 6, which is the Commission's instruction, while at the Supreme Court hearing of 28 October (court-54) the bench said electors on the 2026 roll left off the draft should be allowed the enumeration form or Form 8, with no order reported. The guide's account of the online and offline appeal (page 21 to 23: an 'Appeal Against Order' dashboard, a 2 MB file limit, an automated SMS) and its statement that ECI guidelines prohibit demanding notarised copies were not found in any source the site holds and are not carried. The credits name the researchers and designer; they are not carried, and the byline on the post is used.
